AI revolution can benefit mankind if done in the right way. Less work, abundant prosperity for humans, more leisure time. What is the right way? When you replace real workers with bots that require far lower 'salary' then corresponding discount must be accorded to the end product ie. the goods get cheaper. Everything should get cheaper by 70% to 90%. Currently corporations want to cull human workers, save on paying them salaries, and use bots, while keeping product prices the same or more expensive. This is - as common sense shows - unsustainable. A world where human workers have no jobs to earn will not be able to pay current price of goods. It will collapse. But economists and policy makers aren't addressing this issue. They probably haven't even thought about it. Laws must be made to force corporations who cull human workers to automate work, to correspondingly lower their product cost to that exact percentage they are benefiting financially due to the AI. Eventually this will result in normal market competition to see consumer favor the cheaper goods so encourage all corporations to automate, and all prices become cheaper overall. This makes is possible for people to live luxurious lives even by working just a few hours a week. Even though we will earn less money, goods prices will be so cheap we can live well. Of course, no mass transition to AI can sustainably happen unless human population reduces to one fourth or less of current level. Only then can our future generations have a sustainable high quality life. Otherwise it will be better to be dead than live in appalling conditions on the planet that will ensue due to overpopulation.

I get that you are trying to be hopeful with the "you wont lose your job it will just be different", but the problem is that if LLMs get good enough to do the programming side of my job what is left is the boring bits. Like with airplane pilots. If I wanted to fly a plane I would want to actually fly the plane and not go through a safety list and communicate with the air traffic controller only to watch the plane fly it self. Autopilot automated the fun part of the job and left the human with the boring check list parts and the communication. I love programming. I love the problem solving and the creativity required. I dont like reviewing others code or trying to debug why it doesnt work, but if AI was to actually get good that would be what is left of my job. Just endlessly reviewing code written by AIs and taking blame for it when it crashes.
